summary.headline: Vikram Solar FY26 revenue hit a record INR4,800 crore (+40% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 19%, but guided FY27 non-DCR per-watt EBITDA lower at INR1.75–2.
summary.overview: FY26 set records on revenue (INR4,800 crore), volumes (3.3 GW, +76%), EBITDA (INR917 crore, 19% margin) and PAT (INR470 crore, 10% margin), with Q4 revenue of INR1,450 crore and first 1 GW quarterly run rate. Management said Q4 per-watt cost rose INR0.80 against a INR0.60 realisation gain, compressing per-watt EBITDA to about INR2.35. The order book stood at 8.2 GW at 31 March 2026, with distribution orders removed from the book and C&I DCR orders under renegotiation. The company announced a 6 GW wafer-ingot phase at Gangaikondan (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29) and a 15 GWh BESS target by FY30, while the 9 GW TOPCon cell plant has been pushed to a phased commissioning through Q4 FY27 and ramp in Q2 FY28.

financial_highlights.value: 0.03; working capital net debt INR64 crore; no long-term debt

segments.name: Modules
segments.commentary: Q4 production about 1 GW, the highest ever; nameplate 9.5 GW today rising to 15.5 GW after Gangaikondan 6 GW module plant (first output guided June 2026). Cumulative global deployment crossed 10 GW (over 25 million modules).

segments.name: Cells
segments.commentary: No captive cell capacity yet; 9 GW TOPCon Plus cell plant at Gangaikondan targets first cell December 2026 and completion of phases through March 2027, with a further 3 GW in FY28. A 2 GW DCR cell procurement agreement with Jupiter International supports FY27 DCR offtake, weighted to H2.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: 5 GWh cell-to-pack facility targeted by March 2027 (assembly capex about INR150 crore); 7.5 GWh cell phase 1 in FY29 and phase 2 in FY30 against a 15 GWh FY30 target.

segments.name: Wafer-ingot
segments.commentary: 6 GW phase 1 at Gangaikondan approved by the Board (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29 per call, March 2028 in Q&A); the balance 6 GW is at about INR600 crore per GW, with Board approval planned next fiscal.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at about 8 GW (6 GW non-DCR, 2 GW DCR) and FY27 EBITDA of INR1,500–1,600 crore, about 74% above FY26.
Non-DCR volumes guided to INR1.75–2.00 per watt-peak EBITDA on average through FY27; DCR-linked procurement volumes guided to INR2–2.5 per watt.
Per-watt EBITDA guided to about INR5 in FY28 post cell integration, with a further INR1 reduction as more capex comes in; the current level is about INR6 per watt-peak.
Standard nameplate utilisation of 65–70% for modules and 70–75% for cells after FY27 ramp.
Closing FY27 debt guided at about INR3,200 crore (earlier plan INR3,500 crore); FY28-end debt about INR6,500–6,600 crore; interest and DSCR guardrails above 2.5 and net debt/equity below 1.5.
capex_capacity: 9 GW TOPCon cell plant: civil works by September 2026, cleanroom/MEP October 2026, equipment installation October–November, power by Siemens in November, first cell end-December/early January, commissioning through March 2027, ramp in Q2 FY28; total cell capex for 12 GW about INR5,400 crore, mostly spent in FY27 with the last 10% instalment in FY28 (cost up 10% after switching equipment sourcing from Thailand to China).
Gangaikondan 6 GW module plant in final stretch, first output on track for June 2026; Vallam 5 GW built in under nine months.

Wafer-ingot phase 1 of 6 GW at Gangaikondan (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29; Q&A said March 2028), with advances of under INR100 crore in FY27; BESS cell construction from October 2026 over 24 months, FY27 land and initial spend under INR200 crore.
Management expects standard utilisation of 65–70% on modules and 70–75% on cells, on nameplate basis.
Capex to be funded through a mix of debt and equity, and internal accruals; the company expects to fund FY27 BESS and wafer-ingot outflows largely from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: India added 45 GW of solar in FY26 (against a 24 GW target, about 87% above FY25); cumulative base 150 GW. Utility-scale additions were a record 34 GW and rooftop 8.5 GW.

Management sees over 80 GW of grandfathered Non-DCR demand over two years, about 28 GW of live utility-scale DCR tenders and about 25 GW of inherent DCR demand from C&I, KUSUM and rooftop. Management expects DCR demand of 20–25 GW in FY27.

Cell costs rose during FY26 on higher silver prices and removal of China's export VAT rebate. Aluminium rose from $3,100 to $3,600 per ton; EVA cost rose with crude; partly offset by lower cell prices.
Approximately 80% of the order book has cell price pass-through clauses; FY26 per-watt overhead fell 16%.
Q4 realisations rose about INR0.60 per watt-peak while cost rose INR0.80, compressing per-watt EBITDA to about INR2.35 (DCR mandate from June 2026).

Distribution order book (about 1 GW) was removed from the 1.9 GW Q4 order inflow and moved to spot buying; distribution network about 110+ distributors and 550+ dealers/SIs. A US export project of about 0.6 GW was dropped after the IPP found it unviable.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 1 GW distribution order book removed, and does the 1.9 GW order inflow include distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflow excludes distribution; the recurring distributor order book moved to spot buying as volumes shift to DCR and outsourced cell supply. Distribution was about 20% of Non-DCR volumes last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per watt-peak in Q4 and in the non-DCR business?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 per-watt EBITDA was about INR2.35, with non-DCR volumes guided at INR1.75–2 on average for FY27 and about INR5 for FY28 post cell integration (current about INR6).

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and order plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8 GW of production in FY27 (2 GW DCR, 6 GW non-DCR) against 8.2 GW order book at March 2026, of which 6 GW goes out in FY27 leaving 1.2 GW, with the rest to be won from the 87 GW grandfathered Non-DCR pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt trajectory and interest outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing FY27 debt guided at about INR3,200 crore and FY28 at INR6,500–6,600 crore; interest on construction projects is capitalised until commissioning, so P&L impact is deferred.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling the US export orders and where would it source cells?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports to the US have slowed to near zero since November; about 1 GW of export orders are with long-standing IPPs and are being executed via cells sourced from North Africa, with EU, Australia and Middle East also explored.

qa_highlights.question: How are silver and silicon cost increases passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: MSAs allow pass-through of cell cost and dollar appreciation to the extent of about 80% of the order book; future pass-through depends on the market once cell and wafer-ingot capacity comes in.

risks_watch: Per-watt EBITDA compression: Q4 cost rose INR0.80 vs realisation gain INR0.60, and FY27 non-DCR guidance is INR1.75–2, well below FY26 levels.

Execution risk on 9 GW cell plant (first cell targeted end-December 2026, ramp Q2 FY28) and 6 GW Gangaikondan module plant (June 2026); a sizable part of FY27 volume relies on a third-party 2 GW DCR cell supply.
Order book quality: about 1 GW distribution orders removed, C&I DCR orders under renegotiation, and US export order risk.
Rising interest and working capital needs with Vallam inventory; debt guardrails (DSCR above 2.5, net debt/equity below 1.5) and the INR6,500–6,600 crore FY28 debt level.
Raw material and silver cost pass-through (about 80% of order book) and cell price competition from domestic capacity additions.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on sector growth and integration, with the most specific numbers on FY26 records and FY27 guidance. Less specific or deferring on pricing (2 GW Jupiter procurement commercials not disclosed), US export orders and pass-through terms beyond the current 80% coverage.
key_quotes: The order inflow does not include distribution. We have taken that out of order booking format.
Yes, so when we spoke about a debt level of INR3,500 crores, the plan was to have an entire 12 gigawatt of cell in place, which we have now phased it into 9 plus 3.
Approximately 80% of our order book carries cell price pass-through clauses, insulating the P&L from any input volatility.
So that INR0.20 Additional incremental cost has dented the per-EBITDA-watt-peak to that extent and hence you could see a slight percentage impact on the EBITDA margin level.

Our working assumption is that the sector will stabilize around an 80 to 100 gigawatt of nameplate fully integrated sustainable capacity held by a small group of serious full-stack players, and the total addressable market is heading towards a similar number.

adds.what: 9 GW TOPCon cell plant at Gangaikondan (phased, first cell Dec 2026, commissioning through Mar 2027)
6 GW module plant at Gangaikondan (first output guided June 2026)
6 GW wafer-ingot phase 1 at Gangaikondan (commissioning FY29; Q&A said Mar 2028)

growth.why: FY27 guided to 7.5-8 GW production and INR1,500-1,600 crore EBITDA (~74% above FY26), backed by an 8.2 GW order book and 6 GW module plant due June 2026, but the 9 GW cell plant slips to phased commissioning through March 2027 and FY27 per-watt EBITDA is guided lower at INR1.75-2.00 non-DCR.
